source_locations.intake: Published pages 2931–2955 correspond to PDF pages 1–25. Main discussion and Funding end on page 24, before the supplementary listing at y=166.43. The supplement is a separate file and is excluded.
source_locations.risks_and_weights: Page 3: client losses f_k, risks F_k=E_Pk f_k, heterogeneous P_k, positive weights summing to one, federated risk (1), minimizer theta_K* (2), balanced weights b1<=K*w_k<=b2. Local samples are IID and arrive sequentially; all clients contribute T observations. Full-sample M-estimator (4) is an efficiency benchmark.
source_locations.geometry: Page 4: spectral/Frobenius norms, PSD order, ones/identity/J notation, closed convex parameter space Phi, its diameter R_d, metric projection and its columnwise matrix extension.
source_locations.network: Pages 4–6: undirected client graph with self-loops, symmetric nonnegative row-stochastic connection matrix, optional MH example (5), Assumption 2.1 uniform spectral contraction rho<1 and centralized rho=0 case.
source_locations.algorithm: Page 5: matrix of local estimates, weighted gradient matrix (6) with factor K, shared initialization, projected local SGD with right multiplication by C every tau steps. Full update rule is in main text despite an external algorithm summary.
source_locations.averages: Page 5: distinguish spatial mean, per-client temporal mean and joint spatial-temporal PR average. They are unweighted averages of estimates, while gradients carry the preassigned client weights.
source_locations.step_sizes: Page 7: Assumption 2.2 eta_t=D*(t+gamma)^(-alpha), D,gamma>0, 1/2<alpha<=1. Classical nondistributed SGD results on pages 6–7 are background, not additional Theorem environments.
source_locations.noise_and_smoothness: Pages 7–8: Assumption 3.1 gradient-noise moments through order 2v, with v=1 versus v=2 selected in the theorem; Assumption 3.2 convex L-smooth population risks; Assumption 3.3 weighted gradient heterogeneity kappa and gradient bound B at theta_K*.
source_locations.consensus: Page 8: Lemma 1 supplies the two constants B_MSE and B_CE and states its assumptions explicitly. Theorem 1 contains full Q and delta definitions with domain branches; preserve the local Lemma passage as referenced context without adding it to the theorem inventory.
source_locations.curvature: Pages 9–10: complete Assumption 3.4 with strong-convexity branch and bounded-domain generalized self-concordance branch (all three clauses). Equation (17) defines mu_Rd using L, mu, mu_star, B_G and R_d.
source_locations.mse: Page 10: Theorem 2 supplies its error sequence, constants c1/c2, conditional rate constants v1/v2 and fixed-K almost-sure conclusion. Later references to its assumptions must not turn that fixed-K conclusion into a premise for growing-K theorems.
source_locations.clt_assumptions: Pages 11–12: Assumption 4.1 L-average smoothness of individual stochastic losses; Assumption 4.2 nondegenerate client gradient-noise covariance and aggregated (2+delta) moment; Assumption 4.3 population Hessian Lipschitz continuity. Theorem 3 defines H and S.
source_locations.covariance: Pages 12–13: S=K*sum_k w_k^2*S_k, centered local gradient covariance (22), weighted aggregation (23). Preserve centering because client gradients at the federated target need not vanish.
source_locations.smooth_hessian: Page 13: nondecreasing a:N+->N+, trailing-window client Hessian average evaluated at local temporal means (24), weighted H aggregation, full stochastic-Hessian Assumption 4.4. Theorem 4 adds K*a(T)->infinity and its complete continuation on page 14.
source_locations.regression_hessian: Pages 14–15: nondistributed motivating regression, normalization C(T,alpha) (29), eigenvalue clipping (30). Decentralized estimator uses the three time-segment functions (31), centered gradients from a separate final segment, Z/V formulas and B(T1,T2,alpha). Theorem 5 concerns the thresholded estimator and expected Frobenius norm.
source_locations.one_step: Page 16: one-step estimator (33) uses the alpha=1 PR average and the weighted average of already computed gradients at each local previous iterate, corrected with the smooth Hessian estimate (24). Theorem 6 on page 17 requires T and K to diverge in its consequence. Corollary 1 and sparse-network supplementary results stay outside the inventory.

source_issues_to_archive: Page 4 defines J=d^{-1}*1_d*1_d^T, but the right-centering matrix in Theta_hat_t*(I-J) must act on K client columns. Page 6 explicitly uses K^{-1}*1_K*1_K^T. Preserve both source passages and record the dimension mismatch; do not silently replace d by K inside the quoted definition.

Assumption 2.1 permits rho=0, and Theorem 1 evaluates delta at rho^(1/tau) and its square, while its printed delta definition says a in (0,1). The following remark uses the natural a=0 interpretation. Preserve the open domain and document that extension separately.

Theorem 1 at t=tau invokes eta_floor((t-tau+1)/2)=eta_0 although Assumption 2.2 introduces the sequence for t>=1. An empty sum occurs for tau=1. Record these finite-index conventions rather than silently adding values.

The remark after Theorem 1 changes the order of delta arguments and calls it (14), although equation (14) is the curvature condition. Keep the theorem formula delta(t,a,tau) and distinguish the remark typo.

Assumption 3.4(ii) prints phi triple-prime at t and phi double-prime at u without a full relation or quantifier for t; it also omits an absolute value on the third derivative. Preserve the original condition and record its ambiguity rather than substituting a standard self-concordance definition.

Assumption 3.4 has alternative strong-convexity and bounded-domain generalized self-concordance cases. Do not require the bounded-domain assumptions jointly with the positive-mu case. Theorem 5 separately requires a bounded domain in all cases.

Theorems 3, 4 and 6 refer to assumptions of Theorem 2. Resolve the common assumptions and retain its part-(ii) conditional step-size restrictions as referenced context; inspect the source carefully before deciding their scope. Do not import its fixed-K almost-sure conclusion as a premise.

Theorem 5 explicitly uses v=2 and lists 3.3–3.4 without 3.2. It nevertheless assumes 4.1, described by the author as stronger smoothness. Preserve the printed list; do not insert an unstated numbered assumption merely to match the other theorems.

Page 3 specifies IID observations within each client, while the covariance aggregation on page 12 uses the no-cross-client-covariance formula. Check whether cross-client independence is explicitly stated elsewhere in the main text; record any missing joint-sampling premise rather than inventing it.

Assumption 4.2 mixes notation for aggregated noise epsilon(theta) and epsilon(theta;xi^k), though epsilon(theta) itself sums noises from all clients. Retain its original variables and record the binding issue.

Equation (22) uses gradients at local estimate theta_hat_t^k and data xi_t^k with t=0..T-1; the update (6) uses theta_hat_(t-1)^k and xi_t^k with t>=1. Retain the original covariance-estimator indexing and inspect the time-zero/data-reuse issue.

The trailing-window Hessian estimator (24) uses a(T) observations but only states that a is positive integer-valued and nondecreasing; a(T)<=T is not explicit. Its local temporal mean also reaches index zero when the window spans all observations. Preserve the formula and note any undefined early indices.

In (31), r1+r2+r3=T is imposed, but for alpha=1 the printed r1=T^(1-zeta)/C2 and r2=T/C3, r3=T/C4 with fixed constants cannot sum to T for all T. Integer rounding is also unspecified. Preserve the original formulas without silently changing constants or a segment.

Thresholded V clips eigenvalues to [delta,1/delta] for a small fixed delta>0. The source does not explicitly state a relation between that interval and the limiting spectrum in the theorem. Record that limitation rather than assuming clipping becomes asymptotically inactive.

The regression Hessian estimator Z*V^{-1} need not be symmetric at finite T. The later sandwich formula repeats its inverse without a transpose, as printed. Keep original formulas and distinguish an estimator definition from a claim of finite-sample symmetry.

Equation (33) uses lowercase f_k with a data argument, but Theorem 6 prints uppercase F_k(theta_K*;xi_t^k), although F_k was defined as a population risk with only a parameter argument. Preserve the printed theorem and record the apparent notation error separately.

Theorem 6 expansion has remainder O_p(sqrt(K/T)+1/sqrt(K)); its CLT consequence requires both K and T to diverge. Do not extend it to fixed K based on the PR theorem, which permits fixed K under a different step-size regime.

The external supplement contains algorithm summaries, proofs and sparse-network variants. Main-text algorithm definitions are available and should be used directly. Do not read supplement bodies or add their results to the main-text theorem inventory.
